statement.p: Let f(x) = x^{2}+7x-14 Use the second derivative test to find any local maxima and minima.
First, find the critical point. Enter the x-value below.
Then find the value of the second derivative at that x-values.
If the function has a local maximum at that value, enter MAX. If it has a local minimum, enter MIN.

solution.p: To find the critical points, take the derivative and set it equal to 0 (or where it doesn't exist). f'(x)=2x+7=0 so the critical point is x= \frac{-7}{2\cdot 1} = -3.5.
The second derivative is f''(x)=2. So evaluating that at the critical point gives f''(-3.5)=2 That means that f has a local \text{MIN} at x=-3.5.
